description: We are Beatless Beetles, a hands-on team with skills in web development, data handling, and project management. Passionate about space tech, we are building a clean and functional solution for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We work fast and value simple communication. If you are passioned we would love to collaborate with you.
summary:
Space Mission Design & Simulation Game for Aerospace Engineering Design: Space mission design is transformed into an interactive space mission design and simulation game for aerospace engineering design. In the game, players design and build a space mission while making decisions with many interrelated constraints such as science goals, spacecraft resources, energy, mass, communication, cost, and environment.

In contrast to a purely didactical presentation of all aspects of space mission design, our simulation allows users to see the impact of one engineering decision in the context of the entire mission. For example, adding more scientific instruments to a space mission increases its scientific potential but also puts a strain on mass, energy, communication etc.

The systems thinking involved in space mission design will be facilitated by the use of simplified physical models, NASA data, and interactive game mechanics. This will be particularly beneficial to students and aspiring engineers who do not have access to realistic mission planning tools and experiences.

Our aim is to provide a simple insight into the workings of space missions and the hard decisions that have to be made in order to succeed or fail.
details:
The project is an interactive space mission design and simulation game. It allows users to experience how interconnected decisions in space mission design and operations are.

Players start a space mission by choosing a number of objectives. Then in the engineering phase, players design a space craft and choose the appropriate scientific instruments. They also have to choose between mass and energy, choose a communication system, determine a budget and a number of mission conditions. In the end the player has to assess the success of his space mission.

To achieve this, the project uses a combination of real space-mission concepts and NASA open data and simplified mathematical models to represent complex engineering relationships. The project is written in Python for the core calculation and simulation logic, JavaScript for the dynamic web pages and interactive components, and Figma and 3D design software for the game’s user interface design.

Our main approach for turning systems engineering into an interactive experience around decisions is to allow players to make decisions themselves instead of only being informed about a space craft and a space mission.

We weighed factors of scientific fidelity, game balance, accessibility, technical feasibility, and time. Our goal is to facilitate systems thinking in aerospace mission design and make this complex space of work more intuitive for students and future engineers.
